name: Sionna Visualizer
what_it_is: A full-stack web dashboard that wraps NVIDIA Sionna (open-source 6G simulation library) in a browser interface, turning raw simulation output into interactive, publication-ready charts with export and sharing capabilities. It supports AWGN BER, beam pattern, path loss, channel capacity, and modulation comparison simulations without requiring users to write code.
components: Angular 17 frontend (Angular Material, Chart.js, D3.js, ng2-charts, JWT auth)
Java Spring Boot 3 backend (REST API, Spring Security, JWT, Hibernate, SimulationService, ConcurrentHashMap cache, circuit breaker, Spring Actuator)
Python 3.10 FastAPI bridge (NVIDIA Sionna SDK, tracemalloc, ColormapService)
PostgreSQL database (simulation results, performance metadata, API keys, users)
protocols: HTTP (Spring Boot to Python FastAPI bridge)
OFDM (underlying channel model in Sionna simulations)
measurement: BER vs SNR curves (BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, 64QAM — theoretical and Monte Carlo)
Beam pattern polar charts (ULA antenna, 8/16/32/64 antennas, 28/39/60/77 GHz)
Path loss per-ray FSPL (bar chart, scatter chart, delay chart, data table)
Channel capacity via Shannon theorem C = B × log2(1 + SNR) with 4 bandwidth curves
Simulation performance metadata: duration (ms), memory (MB), CPU/GPU utilization, Sionna version
configuration: Environment variables via .env file (SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL, SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME, SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET, JWT_EXPIRATION, PYTHON_BRIDGE_URL)
docker-compose.yml defines 4 services: postgres, python-bridge, backend, frontend
SNR range: snrMin, snrMax, snrSteps parameters
7 colormap palettes: Viridis, Grayscale, colorblind-safe Publication, and others
Spring JPA DDL auto mode set via SPRING_JPA_HIBERNATE_DDL_AUTO
fault_injection: Circuit breaker on Python bridge — Spring Boot handles FastAPI failures gracefully and reports bridge status
Rate limiting: 10 simulations/min per IP (protects Python bridge from overload)
Railway warmup endpoint (/warmup) prevents cold starts on the Python bridge
Spring Actuator health endpoint exposes python-bridge: warm/cold indicator
modes: Docker Compose mode: docker-compose up starts all 4 services locally on ports 4200, 8080, 8001, 5432
Manual mode: three separate terminals for python-bridge (uvicorn port 8001), backend (Spring Boot port 8080), frontend (ng serve port 4200)
Cloud/production mode: Railway (backend + Python bridge + PostgreSQL) + Vercel (frontend) with GitHub Actions auto-deploy
Authenticated mode: JWT login/register required for simulation history, API key management, bulk export
Public/unauthenticated mode: shareable public links per simulation (no login needed for recipient), public REST API with API key
constraints: Requires NVIDIA Sionna SDK installed in the Python bridge container — GPU acceleration is optional but Sionna has TensorFlow/GPU dependencies that significantly increase image size and startup time
Public REST API is rate-limited to 100 requests/day per API key; simulation endpoint requires a pre-issued API key from the dashboard
Railway free tier causes cold starts on the Python bridge unless the /warmup endpoint is polled; the docker-compose setup has no equivalent keep-alive mechanism
Simulation caching (ConcurrentHashMap) is in-memory and non-persistent — cache is lost on backend restart, so identical parameters incur full re-computation after a restart
PostgreSQL credentials must be provided via .env before docker-compose up — the postgres service will fail to initialize if SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME or SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD are missing
docker_services: postgres — image: postgres:15, port 5432:5432, volume postgres_data, env: POSTGRES_DB=sionna_visualizer + credentials from env
backend — build: ./backend/Dockerfile, port 8080:8080, depends_on: postgres + python-bridge, env: datasource URL/credentials, JWT config, PYTHON_BRIDGE_URL, DDL auto
notable_absences: No GPU/CUDA configuration exposed in docker-compose.yml — Sionna GPU acceleration is not wired into the compose setup
No message queue or async job system — simulations are synchronous HTTP calls from Spring Boot to FastAPI, blocking the request thread
No horizontal scaling configuration — single-instance Python bridge with no worker pool or load balancing
No persistent cache layer (e.g., Redis) — simulation cache is purely in-memory ConcurrentHashMap
No WebSocket or streaming — simulation progress is not streamed; client waits for full HTTP response
